evals.prompt: I have a Preact app and someone suggested switching the whole codebase to `preact/compat` by default to avoid migration issues. Is that the right default? Show a safer integration pattern if we only need one React-only widget library.
evals.expected_output: Rejects compat-by-default, explains tradeoffs, and provides an isolated compat boundary pattern for the React-only dependency.
expectations: States that `preact/compat` should not be the default architecture choice.
Explains explicit tradeoffs (ecosystem compatibility vs size/debugging/assumption risks).
Shows compat isolated to a boundary module/component rather than app-wide default.

evals.expected_output: Replaces index key with a stable identity key and explains why index keys break under reorder/insert/remove operations.
expectations: Replaces `key={idx}` with a stable domain key (`key={it.id}`).
Explains behavioral risk from index keys when list order changes.
Keeps the fix minimal and focused.
